cases.intent: Map hole diameter, centre location, datum offsets, pattern symmetry and plate thickness to feasible, distinct observation paths before and after the length intervention.

Map declared frame/post/beam/tie/gusset interfaces to evidence paths that can actually be performed in the assembled state.

cases.intent: Select a feasible measurement method whose uncertainty can resolve the exact case-specific tolerance/decision boundary, without assuming a universal uncertainty ratio.

power state and safe test conditions

cases.intent: Propose a replacement/service path that retains article identity and registration or explicitly reopens datum, alignment and conformity evidence after replacement.
Reject a claimed post-closure cavity measurement path when no inspection opening, probe path or alternate justified method exists.

cases.intent: Reject a numeric alignment/conformance conclusion when the calibration reference is stale, missing or bound to another instrument.

cases.intent: Return Unknown or request a new measurement where the available logical netlist does not establish physical observability or permit a unique fault diagnosis.
cases.seeded_fault: Ask for a physical board test result from a logical netlist-only fixture with no routed board, test points or instrument profile.

cases.intent: Reject or qualify a proposed measurement whose contact force or setup disturbance changes the quantity being measured beyond the declared model envelope.
cases.seeded_fault: Use a high-force contact measurement on a thin/compliant feature without modelling the induced deformation.

limitations: All cases are public authoring blueprints, not adjudicated gold fixtures or scored tasks.
The referenced CAD and assembly objects are synthetic development fixtures. Their materialization does not establish instrument or measurement-system capability.
ECAD-P01 is a logical netlist only, not a routed PCB; physical testability is intentionally Unknown without additional EDA and instrumentation artifacts.
No real article, calibration certificate, instrument, supplier or production record is included.
No measurement plan proposal is evidence admission, engineering approval, product qualification or physical execution authority.

ISO 10360-2:2009 is scoped to Cartesian CMMs using contacting discrete-point probing for linear dimensions; it is not a generic optical-scanner, laser tracker, CT or non-Cartesian instrument qualification rule.
ISO 14253-1:2017 decision rules apply to in-scope quantity-valued characteristics/specifications and take measurement uncertainty into account; no universal uncertainty-to-tolerance ratio is assumed.
JCGM guidance supports measurement-model and uncertainty reasoning but does not establish the capability, calibration, repeatability or fitness of any actual fixture/instrument.

external_benchmark_context.name: Physical-Engineering's Last Exam
external_benchmark_context.run_protocol: Three runs per model+harness pair; six-hour per-task limit; highest available reasoning effort; official Claude Opus 5.5 rubric judge.
external_benchmark_context.comparability_boundary: This all-85 run is distinct from the 29-task public development board, 56-task hidden board and competition artifact submission. Scores are complete model+harness systems and include LLM-graded rubric tasks.

external_benchmark_context.name: Physical-Engineering's Last Exam — public development
external_benchmark_context.run_protocol: Three runs per model+harness pair; six-hour per-task limit; official development rubric.
external_benchmark_context.comparability_boundary: Only compare against this same 29-task split and protocol. Not comparable to PLE 56-task hidden, all-85 or committed-artifact entry scores. Harness effects are material; preserve the exact model+harness pair.

external_benchmark_context.name: Parametric CAD Bench V3
external_benchmark_context.run_protocol: Harbor 0.23.0; FreeCAD 1.1.0; one attempt per task; four-way concurrency; zero retries; separate programmatic validator.
external_benchmark_context.comparability_boundary: One complete public cohort with a continuous geometry/specification reward. The displayed CI is task-score uncertainty; this is not a manufacturability, metrology, requalification or physical-safety benchmark. Total run cost is USD 573.94/100 = USD 5.7394 per task.

external_benchmark_context.name: BenchCAD 2.0 Core
external_benchmark_context.run_protocol: 30 rounds per case; reasoning not carried between rounds; per-task sandbox; automatic geometry/topology/assembly-placement/ECAD-connectivity scoring.
external_benchmark_context.comparability_boundary: Do not compare v2.0 with v2.1. The score covers CAD geometry/topology, assembly placement and board connectivity, not manufacturing readiness, uncertainty, inspection access, lifecycle requalification or physical performance.

external_benchmark_context.name: CADWorld — Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon CAD
external_benchmark_context.run_protocol: Live benchmark page reports 14 evaluated agents; 100 GUI steps per task; task-specific executable checks on saved FreeCAD artifacts. Extended-run board and original seven-agent paper snapshot are different evaluation snapshots.
external_benchmark_context.comparability_boundary: The live page's 87.0% expert reference is a single-trial expert pass, not an estimated human population mean. The original September paper reports a different seven-agent snapshot with a 17.5% strongest agent. Do not merge the snapshots. The benchmark includes measurement and manufacturing workflows but does not score full claim-to-evidence-path validity, calibration/uncertainty correctness or post-service requalification.
